verified_continuation_certificate_v1.py was given the hardest scrutiny per charter. It is NOT a vacuous gate: 20+ refusal paths in its passing suite are driven by real byte tampering (resealed body, opaque dependency, drifted manifest bytes, forged Python object, production authority mode, primitive-interval family), and the happy path also succeeds. It performs real work on real inputs: canonical re-emit equality, envelope self-hash, manifest SHA vs binding, two Merkle recomputations, per-dependency SHA reopen, binary64-hex-vs-scalar bit equality, and hard-constraint satisfaction.

pytest.tail: source module, not a test file; its dedicated suite (test_taskspace_receding_horizon_controller_v1.py) reports 30 passed in 0.33s

findings.what: CoverageStatus Literal (L63-68) advertises "CERTIFIED_DOMINATED", but ActionFamilyScaleCoverageV1.__post_init__ (L583-592) raises unconditionally whenever that value is supplied. The type surface therefore names a state the code can never produce.
findings.fix: Drop CERTIFIED_DOMINATED from the Literal, or annotate the alias as reserved-and-currently-refused so a reader does not build against an unreachable state.

findings.what: `cross_scale_scan_complete` is a property whose body is `return True` with no runtime check. The vocabulary invariant it names is actually enforced in __post_init__ (L726). The name reads as a check being performed at call time.
findings.fix: Rename to family_scale_vocabulary_declared, or re-assert `set(coverage_by_cell) == expected_cells` inside the property.

findings.what: `enumeration_complete` docstring claims "Every manifest leaf is measured or covered by reverified proof bytes", but the body only re-runs certificate byte reverification. The partition check that actually establishes the claim (L743, `measured_ids | certificate_ids != set(manifest_by_id)`) is not re-run.
findings.fix: Re-assert the measured-plus-certified partition inside the property so its docstring and its body agree.

findings.what: `_functional_quotient` representatives are computed but never consumed by the value computation: L1080 iterates `hard_admissible`, not `quotient_rows`. Only `representative_count` reaches the output (L1405). The numeric result is identical (min over a class equals min over its members), but a reader can reasonably assume the quotient prunes the decision.
findings.fix: State in the docstring that the quotient is telemetry-only, or feed representatives into the value loop so the code matches the framing.

findings.what: `reverified_continuation_certificates` re-runs full proof-byte reverification on every property access; it is read at least four times per decision (L723 __post_init__, L844 enumeration_complete, L880 identity_sha256, L1053 select_receding_horizon_action_v1). Deliberate ("Python objects are not cryptographic capabilities") but the cost is O(bundles x accesses).
findings.fix: No correctness change needed. Consider an explicit single reverify call site whose result is threaded, with the property retained as the durable boundary.

findings.what: `cell_measurements[cell] != measurement` compares a tuple of measured floats with exact !=. The semantic here is identity consistency (equal evaluator-cell identity must imply identical measurements), so exact comparison is correct, but -0.0 and 0.0 compare equal and would not be caught.
findings.fix: If bit-identity is the intent, compare float(...).hex() pairs instead of the raw floats.

findings.what: test_duplicate_key_nan_and_huge_integer_proofs_fail_closed feeds `{"schema": 999...}` at the envelope top level. That payload is refused by the envelope FIELD-SET check (_require_exact_fields, L1195 of the module), never by the _MAX_PROOF_INTEGER bound the test name implies. The test asserts only the exception class, so the signed-64-bit integer guard is never actually exercised.
findings.fix: Put the oversized integer in `subtree_cardinality` inside a resealed proof body and add `match="signed-64-bit"` so the bound is the thing under test.

pytest.tail: source module, not a test file; its dedicated suite (test_verified_continuation_certificate_v1.py) reports 30 passed in 0.31s

findings.what: The verifier proves the covered leaf set is a SUBSET of the reopened manifest (L1251) and that every covered leaf shares the bound first_action_id and support hyperedge (L1254-1261). It does NOT prove the covered set is EXHAUSTIVE for that branch. An omitted worse leaf would raise the claimed `terminal_lower_bound` (which is min over the covered leaves, L1326-1335) without any refusal. Exhaustiveness is delegated entirely to the caller-supplied context.expected_covered_terminal_leaf_ids. The composed system IS sound today because CompleteActionUniverseV1.__post_init__ enforces the partition (controller L743, `measured_ids | certificate_ids != set(manifest_by_id)`), but the verifier is exported in __all__ and any other consumer gets a bound only as strong as its own context.
findings.fix: Inside verify_continuation_proof_bytes, derive the branch leaf set from the already-reopened manifest -- all manifest leaves whose first_action_id and support_hyperedge_sha256 equal the binding's -- and refuse if covered_leaf_ids is a proper subset. Failing that, add an explicit caller-obligation note to the module docstring and to the public function's docstring.

findings.what: _require_authority_axis records at the site that the hardware_substrate leg is OWED for PRODUCTION_CONTEST_CPU/CUDA (Catalog #127). Currently unreachable because L1213 hard-refuses any non-RESEARCH_ADVISORY binding, so there is no live exposure. Flagging so the debt is not lost when the production receipt adapter lands.
findings.fix: No change now. Whoever lands the production receipt adapter must add the substrate leg (or route through validate_exact_eval_evidence) in the SAME landing, exactly as the docstring instructs.

findings.what: ConservativePrimitiveIntervalLeafEvidenceV1.conservative_score_lower_bound is a @property that unconditionally raises. Fail-closed and intentional, but a raising property is surprising to introspection consumers. (dataclasses.asdict does not touch properties, so nothing breaks today.)
findings.fix: Convert to a method named e.g. require_conservative_score_lower_bound() so the raise is visible at the call site.

findings.what: For an empty manifest, expected_id_root is None and L1037 then compares manifest["generated_terminal_leaf_id_root_sha256"] against None -- so an empty manifest must carry JSON null there. The dual sha256-or-null type is easy to misread. Correct and covered (the base-stop test uses an empty manifest), just subtle.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment at L1034 naming the empty-manifest null contract.

pytest.tail: source module, not a test file; its dedicated suite (test_taskspace_chronological_a3_encoder.py) reports 6 passed in 79.17s

findings.what: numerator_sse_after and numerator_sse_reduction (produced in _rank_rows L684-686, surfaced in the receipt as selected_numerator_sse_after / selected_numerator_sse_reduction) are PREDICTED from candidate_numerators -- `constant_rgb.astype(int64) * denominator` for TARGET_CONSTANT_RGB_V1 (L679) or corrected_y1_numerators for CORRECTED_Y1_SUPPORT_COPY_V1 (L681). They are never checked against the actually-decoded output. _strict_verify_compiled_a3 already computes y0_numerators (L813) but uses it ONLY for the non-selected complement (L814-818). The prediction is exact under today's receiver semantics, so no number is wrong right now; the risk is silent drift -- a receiver change would make the receipt's SSE fields wrong while every gate still passes.
findings.fix: In _strict_verify_compiled_a3, also assert equality on the OWNED cells: pass the ranked prefix (or candidate_numerators) in and check y0_numerators[owned_scorer_mask] equals the predicted numerators, raising ChronologicalA3EncoderError on mismatch. The needed array is already materialized, so the added cost is one comparison.

findings.what: EncoderOnlyXIP2GuidanceV1 is exported in __all__ and directly constructible. Its truth labels payload_round_trip_exact and domains_share_identical_xip2_bytes are only checked `is True` in __post_init__ (L637-648) -- never re-derived. The real round-trip verification lives in build_xip2_guidance_targets (L1055-1059). A direct construction therefore asserts a round-trip that was never performed.
findings.fix: Remove the two self-asserting flags from the public dataclass, or re-run the q/scales round-trip inside __post_init__ so the label is earned wherever the object is built.

findings.what: `np.stack(camera, axis=0) if isinstance(camera, list) else camera` -- the list branch is dead. Both call sites (L1117, L1121) pass an already-stacked ndarray.
findings.fix: Delete the isinstance branch.

findings.what: `any(getattr(self, field) is not expected for field, expected in fixed_truth.items())` compares small ints and bools with identity. It works only because CPython interns small ints, and it errs toward refusing (0.0 is not 0 -> raise), so the direction is safe. Still an implementation-detail dependency in a fail-closed truth gate.
findings.fix: Use `getattr(self, field) != expected or type(getattr(self, field)) is not type(expected)` so the intent (exact value AND exact type) is explicit.

The compile function's own docstring does honestly say "this is not ep725 signal-preserving", so this is structure-vs-doc debt, not a false claim.

The adjacent L212 (`binding_sha256 not in packet`) is the load-bearing one.

The surrounding numeric assertions (L378 array_equal on the camera-then-R target, L385-389 factor-2 numerator identity) are what actually verify behavior.

findings.what: `assert receipt["frontier"]["effective_score_to_beat"] == 0.172` hardcodes a frontier score literal. The live .omx/state/canonical_frontier_pointer.json now reads effective_frontier.score = 0.14839100138338618 (contest-CUDA; sub-0.15 landed 2026-08-20), so the test FAILS today -- this is the observed failure, not a hypothesis. It is the CLAUDE.md "Frontier scores are pointer-only -- FORBIDDEN: hardcoded score literals" class reproduced at the test surface: the test breaks on every legitimate frontier move, and its red will be read as a code regression.
findings.fix: Read the expectation from the pointer, exactly as the module under test already does (v15_ms1_coordinate_compatibility.py L370-374): load .omx/state/canonical_frontier_pointer.json and assert receipt["frontier"]["effective_score_to_beat"] == pointer["effective_frontier"]["score"], or assert the selection-rule invariant (score == min(cpu, cuda, upstream)) instead of any number.

findings.what: `assert receipt["economics"]["max_archive_bytes_at_effective_frontier"] == 187_562` is the same staleness one level down: 187_562 is the byte ceiling AT 0.172 (confirmed by the independent pure-function test at L24). At the live 0.14839 frontier the ceiling is smaller, so this assertion is also wrong -- it simply never executes because L45 aborts first. Fixing L45 alone will surface this one.
findings.fix: Derive it: expected = byte_ceiling_for_score(pointer_score, receipt["economics"]["d_seg"], receipt["economics"]["d_pose"]) and assert against that.

findings.what: `if not Path("/Volumes/VertigoDataTier/...").is_file(): return` -- a bare return instead of pytest.skip(). On any host without the VertigoDataTier SSD mounted, this test reports PASS while executing nothing. That is the vacuity==pass class: green is indistinguishable from not-run, and the suite would look clean on CI or a fresh checkout while the entire audit went unexercised.
findings.fix: `pytest.skip("C1 evidence tier not mounted")` so the skip is visible in the report, and record the denominator (skipped vs run) rather than silently passing.

findings.what: SelectedPreimagePair.__post_init__ calls np.shares_memory(frame0, frame1) at L82, but L80-81 already ran _validate_plane on both, which does np.ascontiguousarray(...).copy() (L102). Two fresh copies can never share memory, so the refusal branch at L83 is unreachable dead code. The invariant is still enforced -- by the copy, not by the guard. The test at L37-38 confirms it: passing the SAME source array twice succeeds.
findings.fix: Either move the shares_memory check BEFORE the copies (so an aliased caller is genuinely refused), or delete the dead guard and document that independence is repaired rather than validated.

findings.what: _artifact is called with live_hash=False for the 409,526,925-byte C1 archive: size is checked, SHA-256 is NOT. The returned dict still carries "sha256": expected_sha256 -- the CLAIMED value, presented in the same field name as verified hashes elsewhere in the receipt. The adjacent "live_sha256_verified": False keeps it honest, so this is naming debt rather than a false claim.
findings.fix: Emit the key as "claimed_sha256" when live_hash is False, so a downstream reader cannot mistake it for a verified digest.

findings.what: "current_base_archive_bytes": 339_094 is a hardcoded artifact size with no provenance line and no verification against the actual C0B archive, sitting inside a receipt whose other artifact rows are all size-and-SHA checked.
findings.fix: Derive it from the archive (or from a named receipt), or annotate it with the receipt path it came from.

findings.what: byte_ceiling_for_score doubles `high` without an iteration bound. It terminates for every finite target because the rate term grows without bound, but a pathological target costs on the order of a thousand iterations before the binary search starts.
findings.fix: None required; optionally seed `high` from a closed-form estimate: ceil((target - distortion) * N / 25).

findings.what: AuditPaths.canonical hardcodes the /Volumes/VertigoDataTier evidence root, so audit_coordinate_compatibility is unrunnable on any host without that SSD. It fails closed (CompatibilityAuditError from _read_json), which is the right direction, but the module is machine-bound by construction.
findings.fix: None required. Note only, so that a future CI wiring does not treat the resulting error as a code defect.
